subject: Jakarta onramp: proposed dedicated pool sizing and timing
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@velocita.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 07:14:00 -0700
Subject: Jakarta onramp & dedicated pool ask

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Velocita is targeting a soft launch in Jakarta (AP-Southeast) in late July and the engineering team flagged regional latency + data residency as blockers unless we can get a dedicated pool in the region at launch.

High level ask: can Redwood provision a small dedicated pool in Jakarta for the initial launch window (sustained production traffic anticipated starting 2027-07-25)? Initial estimate from our side: ~700k generated tokens/day (peak ~1.2M), average inference size 200 tokens, and ~80 concurrent active sessions at peak. We also want a short burst buffer for the first 4 weeks.

Attached: preliminary sizing CSV and a short network checklist we need for on-prem/exposed VPC considerations.

What inputs do you need from us to finalize a proposal (GPU count/type, SLA, pricing)? We can fast-track procurement if terms are reasonable.

—Sanjay
Co-founder, Velocita AI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@velocita.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Jakarta onramp & dedicated pool ask

Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask and the data. Looping in Marissa (solutions) and Rishi (capacity ops) so they can propose concrete pool sizing and a timeline. A couple quick clarifying Qs to speed sizing:

- Is the 700k/day the steady-state expected after launch, or does that include launch-week spikes?
- Any regulatory requirement for data to remain in Indonesia (if yes we’ll need Private plan + KMS controls)?
- Preferred models / quantization: are you planning to use an open 34B-style model or something smaller (13B) in Jakarta? That changes token throughput substantively.

If you prefer, Marissa and I can set a 30-min call Monday to run through the prelim numbers and options (hybrid edge vs full dedicated).

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@velocita.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Jakarta onramp & dedicated pool ask

Sanjay / team — quick sizing notes from the solutions side after a brief pass on the CSV:

Assumptions we used:
- Model: 13B-class (sustained bfloat16) — single request median 200 tokens generated
- Average tokens/sec per GPU (13B, bf16): ~1100-1300 tokens/s for generation under Redwood runtime
- Peak concurrency target: 80 active sessions => concurrency units ~= 80 requests in flight (some shorter)
- Latency SLO: <=150ms for prefix + first token, 95th percentile

Prelim recommended pool (jakarta-onramp-v1):
- Sustained: 4 x H100-80GB (sustained optimized) — handles baseline load with room for small growth
- Burst buffer: 2 x A100-80GB for short peaks (first 4 weeks) or for larger model fallbacks
- KV cache enabled + automatic prefix caching for common prompts (saves ~18-25% tokens observed in similar workloads)
- Expected throughput: baseline ~0.9M tokens/day comfortably; with offered burst capacity we can cover the 1.2M peak windows for short periods

Timeline notes:
- Lead time for a new APAC region activation (Jakarta): ~6 weeks for provisioning + network setup + smoke tests (can be accelerated if we can reuse existing APAC PoPs and the customer accepts a slightly lower initial SLA)
- Procurement: we can ship a 90-day committed tranche for the sustained nodes and mark burst nodes as on-demand for the first 30 days

I’ll hand off to Rishi for operational costing, impact to fleet, and any region tradeoffs.

—Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@velocita.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Jakarta onramp & dedicated pool ask

Thanks — adding ops detail and a conservative fleet plan.

Fleet impact and justification:
- Proposed sustained nodes: 4 x H100-80GB (resident in ap-southeast-3 - Jakarta colocation). Each H100 projected to handle ~1.1k tokens/sec for the 13B bf16 profile under Redwood runtime; with 4 nodes we get a baseline capacity headroom for modest traffic growth.
- Burst nodes: 2 x A100-80GB on a short-term reserved window (30 days) to absorb launch-week demand. We can convert to sustained if Velocita needs capacity beyond the trial.
- Networking: ensure customer can meet 10 Gbps egress into our VPC peer; network-checklist-jakarta.pdf has specifics. If not achievable, latency SLOs will degrade.
- Fallback: If capacity is saturated we can route traffic to Singapore pool (ap-southeast-1) with a 20–40ms extra RTT; automatic model fallback to a slightly smaller variant will preserve availability but may change quality.

Costing (ballpark) — committed 90-day tranche:
- 4 x H100 sustained (committed pricing): $11.5/hr per H100 equivalent => ~$46/hr sustained pool
- 2 x A100 ephemeral (burst): $7/hr per A100 => ~$14/hr when active
- Estimated monthly committed spend (sustained only): ~$33k/mo (including base infra, monitoring, and premium SLAs) — final quote will include network egress and reserved capacity discounts in procurement

Operational asks if Velocita signs:
1) Early access to a short prompt set and traffic replay for load testing (we need ~48–72 hours of representative traffic)
2) Signed commit for at least the 90-day sustained tranche to justify region allocation
3) A dedicated network test window for peering and egress validation (we can schedule the test next week)

I can provision a tentative capacity booking subject to approvals — Marissa, Hannah: can we commit to the 6-week lead time if procurement returns signed PO by 2027-05-07?

—Rishi
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Jakarta onramp & dedicated pool ask

Team / Sanjay — thanks for the fast turnaround. Summary and next steps so we’re all aligned:

- Recommended: 4x H100 sustained + 2x A100 burst for initial Jakarta onramp.
- Timeline: 6 weeks from signed PO to smoke tests / readiness (targeting 2027-06-05 smoke if PO signed by 2027-05-07).
- Customer asks: 90-day committed tranche on sustained nodes, burst on-demand for first 30 days.
- Action items:
   * Velocita: confirm model choice (13B vs 34B) and confirm they’ll provide traffic replay or sample prompt set (Sanjay, can you confirm by Tue?)
   * Redwood Sales (me): I’ll route a preliminary commercial (90-day commit) and an initial Statement of Work for review by Monday EOD
   * Capacity/Ops (Rishi): please tentatively block the node capacity and confirm if we can meet lead time assuming no hardware supply issues

If everyone agrees, I’ll send a short commercial term email + HubSpot deal update and attach the SOW draft.

Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sanjay
